robust_repeated_state_result.interpretation: Under the conservative 17-tip binary taxon-concept coding, every AU-nonrejected topology requires at least five erect/upward <-> nodding/downward changes. This is a topology-robust repeated-state lower bound, not yet a population-level count of independent adaptive transitions.

mk_model_sensitivity.rate_scale: changes per unit molecular branch length; accepted tree branch lengths are substitutions/site, not absolute time
mk_model_sensitivity.model_decision: ER is preferred by AICc across all evaluated topology/root-prior cells; ARD provides no supported directional-rate asymmetry.

ancestral_state_sensitivity.interpretation: The root remains essentially equivocal. The analysis does not support calling the ancestral state upward/erect or downward/nodding.

adequacy.interpretation: The fitted ER/ARD models do not fail the preregistered fixed-parameter checks for state balance or minimum-transition count, but passing these checks does not identify a causal ecological mechanism.

decision.next_ecological_gate: same-population sham/reorientation experiment resolving time-window effective pollination versus rain/UV/wetting protection, with antagonist exposure retained as a separate path and filled achenes as the reproductive-fitness endpoint
decision.claim_limit: The robust result is repeated orientation-state change: at least five changes under all six AU-nonrejected topologies. Taxon-concept annotations are not same-voucher or population phenotypes, so repeated-state change must not yet be labelled parallel/convergent adaptation. Direction, ancestral state and ecological cause remain unresolved.
